Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 100, verses 1–11:

**Explanation of the words:**

*Wal-'adiyat* (وَالْعَادِيَاتِ): That is, by the horses that run in raids.

*Dabhan* (ضَبْحًا): That is, they snort *dabhan*. *Dabh* is the sound horses make when they run, that is, when they gallop.

*Fal-muriyati qadhan* (فَالْمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحًا): That is, the horses that strike sparks of fire with their hooves when they travel by night.

*Fal-mughirati subhan* (فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا): That is, the horses that attack the enemy at dawn.

*Fa-atharna bihi naq'an* (فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا): That is, they stir up, by the place of their running, *naq'an*, meaning dust.

*Fa-wasatna bihi jam'an* (فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا): That is, by the dust they penetrate the enemy's host, meaning where the enemy gathers.

*Lakanud* (لَكَنُودٌ): Ungrateful, denying His blessings upon him.

*Lashahid* (لَشَهِيدٌ): That is, he bears witness against himself by his deeds.

*Wa-innahu li-hubb al-khayr* (وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ): That is, wealth.

*Idha bu'thira* (إِذَا بُعْثِرَ): That is, overturned and brought out what is in the graves.

*Wa-husshila ma fi al-sudur* (وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ): Made clear and separated what is in the hearts of faith and disbelief.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The words of the Exalted, ﴿By the racers, panting﴾ through to His words ﴿Does he not know?﴾, contain a great divine oath concerning a great truth that many people are ignorant of: that man disbelieves in his Lord and in His blessings upon him. He counts calamities and forgets blessings and bounties. This is an explanation of what the Exalted swore by: *al-'adiyat dabhan* (the racers panting), which are the horses that make a particular sound other than the familiar neighing. *Fal-muriyati qadhan* (the strikers of sparks): the horses that strike fire with their hooves when they walk over stones at night, and every spark-striking thing is included in this. *Fal-mughirati subhan* (the raiders at dawn): groups of horses ridden by their riders to attack the enemy at morning. His words *fa-atharna bihi naq'an, fa-wasatna bihi jam'an* mean that the horses raise dust, which is the dust and earth raised by their running with their riders, so they penetrate the enemy's host and its battalions, to fight the enemies of God who disbelieve in God and His signs and who meet Him, the corrupters on earth through polytheism and sins. This is what God the Exalted swore by: horses with three attributes, running, striking sparks, and attacking. The sworn-to matter is His words ﴿Indeed, man is to his Lord ungrateful﴾. What is meant by "man" here is the disbeliever, the one ignorant of his Lord, whose soul has not been refined by knowledge of God, of what He loves and what He dislikes, and who has not purified himself by doing what is loved and avoiding what is disliked. God the Exalted swears that this man is ungrateful to his Lord and to His blessings upon him, that is, greatly disbelieving, abundant in mentioning calamities, feeling them, crying out over them, persisting in them, and forgetting the blessings and bounties upon him, so he does not mention them nor thank God for them. *Al-kanud* is *al-kafur* (the ungrateful).

His words, the Exalted, ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾ mean: and indeed God, the Exalted, is a witness to this attribute of man. He informs us of what He knows about man and bears witness against him, just as man is a witness against himself by his deeds and the works of his words and actions, bearing witness against himself of disbelief and denial.

His words ﴿And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense﴾ are another matter God swore by, and it is a description of the ungrateful man: that he is intensely fond of wealth. Wealth is called *khayr* (good) by customary usage, since people have become accustomed to this, and it is also good in that much good is achieved through it when it is spent for the pleasure of God the Exalted.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered, and what is in the breasts is made known, indeed their Lord, that Day, is fully Aware of them?﴾ mean: does man, who disbelieves in his Lord and denies His blessings and kindness to him, and loves wealth most intensely, so that he withholds God's rights in it and earns it by what God has forbidden him, not know? His words ﴿Does he not know, when what is in the graves is scattered﴾ mean: the graves will be overturned and what is in them of humans will be brought out for reckoning and recompense, and they will stand before God the Exalted. What was hidden in the breasts of beliefs and intentions, good and corrupt, will be separated and made clear, and nothing of them will be hidden from God the Exalted, for ﴿indeed their Lord, that Day, is fully Aware of them﴾, as He is Aware today, except that it is the hour of reckoning and recompense. So He mentions in it the knowledge of God the Exalted and His awareness of the outward and inward, the thoughts and the secrets, so nothing of that is hidden from God. Just recompense will be carried out according to this knowledge and this divine awareness.

So if the ungrateful man among people, who loves wealth, knew this and were certain of it, he would correct his conduct, improve his belief, his words and his deeds. Thus the verses are a call to watchfulness of God the Exalted, following faith and steadfastness in obeying Him.

**Guidance from the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Encouragement to jihad and preparation for it, like the horses of yesterday and the jet aircraft of today.
2. An explanation of the truth that man is ungrateful to his Lord and to His blessings upon him: he remembers a calamity when it befalls him and forgets the blessings that surrounded him, except when he believes and does righteous deeds.
3. An explanation that man loves wealth with intense love, except when he is refined by faith and righteous deeds.
4. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.
